name: Djibouti

findings.summary: Phase II of Djibouti Télécom's network expansion and renovation, financed by a China Development Bank loan with Huawei as contractor, supplied core network equipment and expanded GSM capacity; completed June 2007.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: Huawei supplied core network equipment. Pre-2020 and still_current not checked; whether Huawei core remains in Djibouti Télécom's network today is unknown. US$18.29m is the nominal loan amount per AidData; ZTE also issued a loan guarantee. Single opened source.

findings.financier: Bank of China, China Construction Bank, China CITIC Bank (system loans)
findings.summary: Djibouti Télécom signed a landing party agreement with PEACE Cable International Network, a Hengtong subsidiary, to land the PEACE cable in Djibouti; Huawei Marine handled installation and Hengtong manufactured the cable.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: cable supplier and installer are PRC firms. Tier 3 for the signed landing agreement; this run did not confirm that the Djibouti landing is in service (TeleGeography 2022 expected full completion end-2022). Corroboration rests on two trade outlets carrying the same release; reviewer may downgrade.

findings.local_actor: Djibouti Télécom (consortium with Somtel, Hormuud, Telkom Kenya)
findings.summary: The DARE1 cable, manufactured by SubCom for a consortium led by Djibouti Télécom, links Djibouti City with Bosaso, Mogadishu and Mombasa; it entered service in February 2021 with 36 Tbps capacity.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us: SubCom is the equipment supplier. The supplier is named only in the 2019 SubTel Forum piece; Developing Telecoms confirms operation since 2021. US$81m is the consortium's stated investment. Djibouti Télécom plans a Kenya–South Africa extension (work from 2026, RFS 2028; supplier not named).

findings.summary: Djibouti Télécom signed a partnership agreement with Ericsson on 4 December 2024 to deploy 5G in Djibouti; no rollout date was given.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: Ericsson is Swedish. Tier 2 as a partnership agreement without disclosed value. Notable because Huawei was earlier the core vendor (DJI-001) and in Feb 2024 discussed rural 4G/5G antennas with the minister (OperatorWatch, opened, S5-type blog, not cited). Not a reversal of Huawei on the evidence.

findings.summary: PAIX Data Centres announced a joint venture with the Djibouti Sovereign Fund to build JIB1, a 5 MW carrier- and cloud-neutral data centre in Djibouti City, scheduled to open in 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: PAIX, a foreign African operator (Accra, Nairobi; Africa50-backed), is to own land, buildings and equipment; its home jurisdiction and JV equity split were not stated, so domestic share of control is unclear. Tier 1: announcement only; 2026 opening not confirmed.

findings.controller: Djibouti Data Center (JV of Djibouti Télécom and Djibouti Data Center SARL)
findings.summary: Djibouti Data Center, a joint venture of Djibouti Télécom and a group of local and international investors, began commercial colocation and internet-exchange operations in 2013 beside Djibouti Télécom's cable landing station.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic assumed: state telco is a JV partner, but the SARL includes unnamed international investors and the equity split is unknown. DCD 2021 describes it as the only carrier-neutral facility then, so operating at least to 2021; still_current not confirmed for 2026. Both sources on one host, so not corroborated.
